Hyperliquid: best liquidity of any orderbook DEX.

Lighter: first truly innovative success, a “zero-fee” model with costs shifted elsewhere, plus the Robinhood association.

Variational: the MM executes for users, first successful B-book style exchange.

Papertrade: synthetic degeneracy haven, zero-cost and zero-impact execution.

All four are first-mover innovations that turned a new vision into adoption. I am not interested in “farming” something without novelty. There are 20 different perp DEXes claiming to be better, more liquid, faster, bigger, backed by XYZ. Unless I see something novel, I’m not interested.

Recent thoughts on the topic, hope this helps some of you.

tweets.text:
$BTC is holding. $ETH is starting to look vulnerable. 

And that difference matters. Let me do a technical deepdive to give you more insights.

Bitcoin is moving sideways around $80,980. RSI is at 44.6 and price is trading below the 20MA and EMA20, with the 50MA just above. 

The lower Bollinger Band is giving a mild oversold signal, but there’s no real sign of panic: MVRV is at 1.54, SOPR is exactly 1.00, and funding is basically neutral.

One thing that stands out: whales are more cautious than retail. As long as Bitcoin holds above $75K, the broader structure remains relatively intact. Above $83.5K would be the key breakout zone.

Ethereum looks weaker. Price is around $2,361, RSI is at 34.1, and Ethereum is roughly 9% below the 20MA. The $2,318 swing low is currently the thin floor.

Fundamentally, Ethereum looks cheap: MVRV is only 1.09. But the market structure remains weak. The long/short ratio is 2.58 while whale delta is negative. Retail is heavily positioned long while whales appear less convinced, increasing the risk of a downside squeeze.

Bottom line: Bitcoin looks neutral and is waiting for confirmation of the range. Ethereum looks fundamentally cheap, but technically more vulnerable.
